# NL1xxx\: forbidden syntax

The 63 codes of band 1. [Diagnostics](../diagnostics.md) says what a code promises and how a rule's fragment is matched.

## NL1001

The message of an error contains:

```text
… (it aborts rather than unwinding): return a `Result<T, E>` for a failure a caller should handle, or `panic(message)` to end the process
```

## NL1021

The message of an error contains:

```text
`Function` constructor is forbidden in …
```

[`nl1021_function_call.ts`](https://github.com/amritk/nish/blob/main/tests/wordings/nl1021_function_call.ts):

```ts
// NL1021: `Function(...)` called without `new` is refused by its own Phase 0 rule, not by the `new Function` one.
export const main = (): i32 => {
  const s: string = Function("return 1");
  return 0;
};
```

```text
`Function` constructor is forbidden in Nish (no interpreter at runtime)
```

## NL1041

The message of an error contains:

```text

```

[`nl1041_computed_property.ts`](https://github.com/amritk/nish/blob/main/tests/wordings/nl1041_computed_property.ts):

```ts
// NL1041: An object literal's keys are names, because each key is a field slot fixed at compile time.
interface Point {
  x: i32;
}

export const main = (): i32 => {
  const k: string = "x";
  const p: Point = { [k]: 1 };
  return p.x;
};
```

```text
Computed property names are forbidden in Nish (member names are fixed at compile time)
```

## NL1057

The message of an error contains:

```text
… (an import names source this compiler reads, never a resource loaded at run time)
```

[`nl1057_import_attributes.ts`](https://github.com/amritk/nish/blob/main/tests/wordings/nl1057_import_attributes.ts):

```ts
// NL1057: Import attributes describe how a host loads a resource, and an import here only ever names source.
import { one } from "./wordings_lib" with { type: "json" };
```

```text
Import attributes (`with { ... }`) are forbidden in Nish (an import names source this compiler reads, never a resource loaded at run time)
```

## NL1058

The message of an error contains:

```text
… (an export is a declaration, and a declaration has a name; import it by that name)
```

[`nl1058_string_export_name.ts`](https://github.com/amritk/nish/blob/main/tests/wordings/nl1058_string_export_name.ts):

```ts
// NL1058: An export is a declaration's name, so a module export name written as a string names nothing.
import { "one" as uno } from "./wordings_lib";
```

```text
A module export name written as a string is forbidden in Nish (an export is a declaration, and a declaration has a name; import it by that name)
```

## NL1059

The message of an error contains:

```text
… (a module has no top-level code, so there is nothing to defer)
```

[`nl1059_import_defer.ts`](https://github.com/amritk/nish/blob/main/tests/wordings/nl1059_import_defer.ts):

```ts
// NL1059: A module has no top-level code, so `import defer` has no evaluation to postpone.
import defer * as lib from "./wordings_lib";
```

```text
`import defer` is forbidden in Nish (a module has no top-level code, so there is nothing to defer)
```

## NL1060

The message of an error contains:

```text
… (a module has no runtime object; resolve paths at compile time)
```

[`nl1060_import_meta.ts`](https://github.com/amritk/nish/blob/main/tests/wordings/nl1060_import_meta.ts):

```ts
// NL1060: A module has no runtime object for `import.meta` to name; paths are resolved at compile time.
export const main = (): i32 => {
  const url: string = import.meta.url;
  return 0;
};
```

```text
`import.meta` is forbidden in Nish (a module has no runtime object; resolve paths at compile time)
```

## NL1062

The message of an error contains:

```text
`?.` is allowed only in a chain that ends in `??`, whose default stands in when a link is `null`: write `a?.b ?? d`, or narrow with `!== null`
```

[`nl1062_chain_without_default.ts`](https://github.com/amritk/nish/blob/main/tests/wordings/nl1062_chain_without_default.ts):

```ts
// NL1062: a `?.` chain that is not the left operand of `??`.
class Node {
  value: i32 = 1;
}

export const f = (a: Node | null): i32 => a?.value;
```

```text
`?.` is allowed only in a chain that ends in `??`, whose default stands in when a link is `null`: write `a?.b ?? d`, or narrow with `!== null`
```
